Rh(III)-Catalyzed and synergistic dual directing
group-enabled redox-neutral [3+3] annulation
of N-phenoxyacetamides with a-allenols†
Fangyuan Chen, ‡ Junyuan Tang,
 ‡ Yinhui Wei, Jingyuan Tian, Hui Gao, Wei Yi
 *
and Zhi Zhou
 *
By virtue of a-allenols as innovative three-carbon annulation
components, the Rh( III)-catalyzed redox-neutral C–H coupling of
N-phenoxyacetamides witha-allenols has been realized for the assem-
bly of 4-alkylidene chroman-2-ol frameworks via an unusual [3+3]
annulation. This transformation features good functional group toler-
ance, specific regio-/chemoselectivity and potential synthetic utility.
Mechanistic studies reveal that synergistic coordination modes
between the dual directing groups (–ONHAc and –OH) and the
rhodium metal center account for the observed exclusive selectivity.
Due to their remarkable reactivity, allenes have been proven to
be versatile reagents that participate in diversified transforma-
tions including transition metal (TM)-catalysed C–H functiona-
lization for the construction of privileged motifs from readily
available raw materials.
1 Typically, the regio-/chemoselectivity
control represents a major challenge for allene-involved reac-
tions, in which both electronic and steric effects play essential
roles in determining the reaction outcome.
2 As a consequence,
more recently a-allenols equipped with a free hydroxyl group
have been developed as reactive coupling partners (CPs) in
TM-catalysed and directing group (DG)-assisted C–H annula-
tions. The synergistic coordination modes of DGs and –OH
account for the tunable reaction selectivity, giving specific
access to dihydrofurans or [ n+1] annulation products
(Scheme 1a).
3 Despite these impressive advances, further
exploration of novel reaction manifolds of a-allenols to furnish
intriguing structures is still highly desirable.
On the other hand, N-phenoxy amides bearing the –ONHR
moiety have been developed as powerful oxidizing direc-
ting groups (ODGs) for Rh( III)-, Ir( III)-, Co( III)-, Ru( II)- or
Pd(II)-catalysed C–H functionalization,4,5 among which several
hydroxyl group-tethered CPs e.g. propargyl and cyclopropenyl
alcohols were viable substrates to couple with N-phenoxy amides
in a regio- and chemoselective manner. 6 Mechanistic studies
implied that the synergistic coordination effect between the dual
directing groups (DDGs, –ONHR and –OH) and the catalyst metal
centre was the key factor for selectivity control. Encouraged by
these results and in continuation of our interest in developing
DDGs-enabled novel C–Hfunctionalization,

N-phenoxyacetamides witha-allenols for the specific construction
of 4-alkylidene chroman-2-olsvia an unusual [3+3] annulation, in
which the a-allenols work as innovative three-carbon annulation
components (Scheme 1c). Considering the novel reaction mode,
the specific selectivity control as well as the widespread existence
and the potential utility of chroman-2-ol structural motifs in
nature (Scheme 1b),
8 the developed methodology should be of
current interest and have profound synthetic potential.
At the outset of our investigation, N-phenoxyacetamide 1a
was selected as the model substrate to react with a-allenol 2a in
the presence of [Cp*RhCl 2]2. The reaction proceeded smoothly
in DCE with CsOAc being the additive, delivering an intriguing
4-alkylidene chroman-2-ol derivative 3aa via regioselective [3+3]
annulation (Table S1, entry 1, ESI †). Considering the specific
regio-/chemoselectivity, the a-allenol-mediated innovative
annulation mode, and the interesting 4-alkylidene chroman-2-ol
structure of this transformation, we next systematically screen
several experimental parameters to figure out the optimized reac-
tion conditions (see Table S1 in the ESI † for details). Preliminary
screening revealed that the reaction could be finished within 4
hours at an increased temperature, and KOPiv appeared to be an
ideal additive. Most other organic solvents were also compatible
but resulted in relatively lower yields compared with that of DCE.
Control experiments showed that other Rh(
III) species bearing
diﬀerent cyclopentadiene ligands and Ir(III), Ru(II)o rC o (III)c a t a -
lysts all gave inferior results. VariousN-phenoxy amides equipped
with diﬀerent substituents on the nitrogen atom were also
tested and delivered the desired product 3aa smoothly while
N-phenoxytosylamide proved to be ineﬀective.
Having established the optimal reaction conditions, we next
investigated the substrate scope and compatibility for this
reaction (Scheme 2). A series of N-phenoxyacetamides was first
examined to react with a-allenol 2a, the results revealed that
various most commonly encountered functional groups
including alkyl ( 3ba and 3ca), halogen ( 3da–ga), phenyl ( 3ha),
trifluoromethyl (3ia), cyano (3ja)a n de s t e rg r o u p s(3ka) were fully
tolerated for this transformation, delivering the desired
4-alkylidene chroman-2-ols smoothly. It should be noted that, for
N-phenoxyacetamides bearing e lectron-withdrawing groups
(e.g. –CF
3,– C N ,– C O2Me), part of the starting material could be
recovered under the standard conditions, which is probably due to
the strong electronic properties of such substrates and accounts
for the relatively low yields of the corresponding products.
Further exploration illustrated that ortho-a n d meta-substituted
N-phenoxyacetamides participated in this [3+3] annulation reac-
tion smoothly, among which the C–H metallation occurred at the
less hindered site to give the regio-specific products when
meta-substituted N-phenoxyacetamides were employed ( 3la–oa).
The naphthalene substrate was also a viable reactant to afford the
corresponding 3,4-dihydro-2H-benzo[g]chromen-2-ol3pa.R e m a r k -
ably, the dopamine and
L-tyrosine derived N-phenxoyacetamides
underwent the desired coupling with 2a smoothly under the
standard conditions, giving an access to 4-alkylidene chroman-2-ol
3qa and 3ra in decent yields, implying the profound potential of the
developed protocol for the rapid construction of biologically active
moleculesvia late-stage C–H modification.
Subsequently, the generality of this transformation was
further extended with regard to a variety of a-allenols. Diverse
a-allenol substrates bearing diﬀerent alkyl substituents at the a
position were all compatible with the formation of the desired
products (3ab–ad). Other a-allenols equipped with various alkyl
or aryl substituents also participated in this transformation
smoothly, giving access to the corresponding chroman-2-ol
derivatives 3ae–aj. The structure of 3ai was confirmed using
X-ray crystallography (CCDC 2084815 †).

To gain more insight into the reaction mechanism and
probe the role of the hydroxyl group in tuning the reaction
selectivity, a series of experimental mechanistic studies were
carried out. Initially, by employing D
2O as the deuterium
source, deuterium-labeling experiments were conducted and
revealed a reversible C–H metallation. The distinctive deutera-
tion at the allylic position of 3aa suggested a keto–enol tauto-
merization process (Scheme 3a). Additionally, the treatment of
3ea in CD
3OD furnished obvious deuterium incorporation,
which suggested an equilibrium between the ring-opening
ketone fragment and the chroman-2-ol skeleton bearing a
hemiketal moiety. Kinetic isotope studies via both the compe-
titive experiment and two parallel, side-by-side reactions
revealed the primary KIE values of 1.6 and 1.3, demonstrating
that the C–H bond cleavage might not be involved in the rate-
determining step (Scheme 3b). Moreover, a control experiment
using a-allenols4 and 6 led to the formation of 2H-chromen-2-one
5 and diene derivative 7, respectively, which provided adequate
evidence to support that the secondary alcohol moiety was essen-
tial in assembling the chroman-2-ol skeleton (Scheme 3c). Further
exploration was carried out to verify the coordination effect
between –OH and the rhodium metal. As shown in Scheme 3d,
the removal of the hydroxyl group resulted in an inseparable
mixture of complex products, while the allene substrate bearing
a coordinated –NHTs fragment delivered the corresponding
4-alkylidene chroman-2-amide framework 10. These results illu-
strated the crucial role of the coordination effect in tuning the
specific chemoselectivity to afford chromane products.
On the basis of the above experimental studies and the
literature precedent,
10 a plausible catalytic cycle was proposed
for the developed protocol (Scheme 4). With the aid of KOPiv,
the active catalyst was generatedvia anion exchange, followed by a
reversible C–H bond cleavage to form the five-membered rhoda-
cycle A. The following coordination of free hydroxyl groups to
rhodium led to the regioselectiv e insertion of an allene double
bond into the C–Rh bond, giving the Z

Finally, the cyclization of F resulted in the thermodynamically

decrease in yield, implying the practicality of this trans-

In summary, by synergistically employing –ONHAc and –OH
as coordinated DDGs, we have developed the efficient
Rh(III)-catalysed C–H [3+3] annulation of N-phenoxyacetamides
with a-allenols for the specific co nstruction of 4-alkylidene
chroman-2-ols. The distinctive coordination effect between free
hydroxyl groups and the catalyst metal accounted for the observed
regio- and chemoselectivity, thus fulfilling a controllable [3+3]
annulation mode using the a-allenol skeleton as an innovative
three-carbon annulation component. Further exploration of novel
reaction manifolds for allenes in the C–H functionalization field
a n dd e t a i l e dm e c h a n i s t i cstudies are in progress.
